reviews.review:
Surprisingly good bullet heaven, surprising because the art looks just a tiny bit better than one of those "dude learns how to code a video game in three weeks, uses MS Paint to draw it" specials that are all over Steam, but no. The graphics look fine if you zoom in a bit (leave the field of vision on default rather than wider), and they have a good sense of humor to them. Combined with the over the top music, they make this game more charming and unique than you'd expect for the Steam bargain bin.

At first the game feels floaty, but yeah, you're in a boat on water. Your ship should be a little unwieldly, and this is remedied by both holding the X (drift) button when turning, and you can also upgrade turn speed and tightness with in-run powerups and meta powerups. Or choose a ship with a better turning radius. Which leads me into the next point of what this game does well: powerups and unlocks. There's a ton of them, and most of them fit the pirate/nautical theme really well. How about attack parrots circling your boat? Or sending out musical attack notes from a sung pirate shanty? The ships all have very specific strengths compared to one another, which makes you want to choose specific level up powers based on need for your ship. The game is well thought out.

One of the few negatives is the RNG is a bit feast or famine. Kill a boss monster who drops a chest and you can get between 1 and 5 powerups from it, and even more importantly you might get lucky and one of those powerups turns one of your weapons to a continuous fire, and with that you're probably going to go 2x-4x as far as you would have otherwise. But really that's not so bad. There are a lot of boats and captains and powerups to unlock in the meta progression, and I don't want to play this game for 30 hours so give me some magic runs, that's cool.

If you like the genre you'd like this. Fun, humorous, and plays well.
